chapter_title_en: The Might of Three Dao-Arts and the Bashe's Maw
chapter_seo_title: Desolate Era Chapter 412 – Ji Ning’s Primaltwin Unleashes Hell Before a Bashe Ambushes Him
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning’s Primaltwin annihilates the Seven Dharma Kings in a single strike! But a terrifying Primordial Godbeast formation, led by mysterious white-robed assassins, appears to swallow him whole.
og_title: Ji Ning Deletes the Blood God Church’s Elite Team in Seconds
og_description: A masterclass in power scaling: Ji Ning’s top-tier sword formation shatters the enemy’s peak teamwork, only to be met by an even deadlier threat from the shadows.
twitter_title: That moment when a Bashe godbeast shows up to ruin your power fantasy...
twitter_description: Ji Ning wipes the floor with the Seven Dharma Kings, but a legendary snake formation is waiting for its dinner.

lore_anchors.definition: A second body cultivated by a Ki Refiner at the Primal Daoist stage; it shares the same soul and consciousness and can act independently.
A legendary Primordial Godbeast-serpent described in ancient Chinese mythology as being large enough to swallow an elephant.
A sword formation created by a Daofather, perfectly matched with the Li Tian series of swords. It is known for its powerful and elegant area-of-effect attacks.
The highest tier of artificial magic treasure, exclusive to Celestial Immortals. The Qianqiu Sword is a “nearly Purely Yang” weapon, making it the absolute peak of the Immortal grade.
An extraordinarily rare and precious single-use talisman that allows a user to instantly teleport across vast distances, even through spatial seals.
A formless, unstoppable force that tests the cultivator’s Dao-heart directly by entering through the crown of the head; cannot be blocked by any physical or magical defense.
A Chinese social concept representing one’s reputation, status, and dignity in public; losing face can trigger strategic retreat, hostility, or revenge.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why could Ji Ning kill the Seven Dharma Kings so easily?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because he had nine top-grade Immortal-ranked flying swords operating in a coordinated Daofather-created sword formation. This is a “gear-check” moment where his treasure quality and formation art vastly outclassed the enemy’s, creating a power gap that no amount of teamwork could overcome.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the danger Ji Ning felt before the Bashe appeared?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It was his Dao-heart giving him an instinctual warning. Many peak cultivators have this “spider-sense” for danger, which is a product of their deep connection to the Dao and their own will to survive.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn’t Blooddrop run away after his team died?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is a mad, proud villain. He values “face” and believes his treasure ship makes him invincible. His primary goal shifts from defeating Ji Ning to assassinating the Diancai Immortal to salvage some victory and earn credit.
